name: Turing system on a growing domain of one half-stripe (Lengyel-Epstein kinetics)
question: Is the end that holds the peak of the activator inherited when the domain divides below its critical length?
assumptions: the Lengyel-Epstein kinetics of Fig. 8 of the source with its fixed-domain equations under exponential growth (dilution -r u, -r v), one dimension
a domain of one half-stripe, in which the first instability is a polarity; zero flux at both ends
division at L = 0.50 into two halves (the second mode becomes unstable at 0.57)
additive noise of intensity 1e-3 per unit length on both species

provenance.source: K. J. Painter, P. K. Maini and H. G. Othmer, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 96, 5549 (1999), Fig. 8 and Eq. 4
